Can a start capacitor replace a run capacitor?
No. Start and run capacitors have different circuit duties, even when their µF values or case sizes match. Follow the duty and switching arrangement specified by the motor manufacturer.

What details are needed for a dual-run quotation?

How to find the right water pump capacitor size

In a capacitor request, “size” can mean the µF value or the physical dimensions. Find the electrical value first. For an existing pump, read the original capacitor label alongside the motor model and wiring diagram. For a new assembly, use the capacitor requirement supplied with the motor.

A kW or horsepower figure leaves out the motor’s winding design and capacitor arrangement. Two motors with the same output can need different capacitances. Use the specified nominal value instead of converting pump power into µF with a general chart.

Also identify the capacitor’s job in the circuit. CBB60 is a run-capacitor format. A motor with a separate start capacitor needs that part identified separately; a matching µF value does not make the two duties interchangeable.

Oriental Motor’s replacement guidance calls for matching the specified capacitance and rated voltage. It also explains that an incorrect capacitance can reduce torque, cause vibration or overheat the motor. Increasing µF is therefore a change to the motor circuit, not a way to upgrade the pump.

On-time, rest time and the complete cycle

CD60 is an aluminium electrolytic start capacitor. The starting circuit connects it during startup and must disconnect it after its starting role is complete. It is unsuitable for the continuously connected run-capacitor position.

For duty calculations, on-time is the period the capacitor remains connected. Rest time is the period it is disconnected before the next start. Add them to obtain the complete cycle period, measured from one start to the next.

Make that measurement clear when describing an interval. “Three minutes between starts” and “three minutes of rest after disconnection” are different timing requirements. A short timing trace is often clearer than an interval written without a start and end point.

A capacitor can retain charge after power is removed. This procedure is for qualified personnel. Use the equipment service instructions and instrument manual for isolation, approved discharge equipment and verification before handling the terminals.

Compare each reading with its own tolerance limits and the instrument’s stated accuracy. An over-range indication needs a range and setup check before drawing a conclusion about the part.

On the photographed CBB65, 20 µF × 5% gives 1 µF. The lower limit is 20 − 1 = 19 µF; the upper limit is 20 + 1 = 21 µF. The same calculation gives the bands for the CBB60 and CBB61 sample labels in the table.

More µF changes the motor circuit

Capacitance affects current and phase displacement in the auxiliary winding. A larger value can change torque, vibration and heating. For a motor specified at 20 µF, choosing 25 µF to improve starting is an electrical change, not an ordinary like-for-like replacement. Use the motor’s approved value.

Tolerance describes variation around a nominal value. A 20 µF ±5% label gives 19–21 µF; ±10% gives 18–22 µF. A wider tolerance is not permission to order an unrelated nominal value. For dual-run capacitors, preserve the specified value and tolerance of each section.
Capacitor voltage is not the mains supply voltage

VAC is the capacitor’s rated AC voltage. The voltage across a capacitor in the motor circuit can differ from the line voltage. A motor supplied at a lower voltage can therefore still specify a 450 VAC run capacitor. Select from the motor requirement rather than reducing the capacitor rating to the supply value.

Questions about 370 versus 440 VAC, or 440 versus 450 VAC, need the full replacement specification. A higher printed voltage does not resolve differences in construction, operation class, temperature or duty. Never infer starting-duty compatibility from the voltage alone.
The electrical match still needs an installed fit

A run capacitor can use a round or oval case, wire leads or quick-connect terminals. The replacement must fit the bracket and provide the right connection geometry with the connector installed. Temperature category and any required design-life class stay tied to the selected model and its rated conditions.

For an approved substitution, retain the original equipment reference beside the new model datasheet and drawing. That creates a usable cross-reference for future orders. A list containing only µF and VAC loses the connection, mounting and operating limits that made the replacement suitable.

CBB60 is a cylindrical film motor run capacitor. Choose its capacitance from the motor specification, then match the rated AC voltage, operating conditions and physical installation. A CBB60 designation identifies the family; it does not identify a complete replacement part.
Where does a CBB60 belong?

In a capacitor-run single-phase motor, the capacitor remains connected to the auxiliary winding during operation. CBB60 applications include water pumps and selected washing-machine, blower and smoke-exhaust motors designed for this arrangement. An inverter-driven motor or a motor with a different starting circuit needs its own specified component.

The HAN XING catalogue describes metallized polypropylene film in an insulated plastic case. Its published family range is 2–100 µF and 110–450 VAC. Those endpoints describe the catalogue range; the quoted model determines the available combination of capacitance, voltage and case.
25 µF and 35 µF are different motor requirements

The supplied wired HAN XING sample is marked 35 µF ±5%, 450 VAC and 50/60 Hz. The horizontal sample in photograph P003 is 25 µF, also at 450 VAC. A motor specified for 25 µF still requires that value even if the 35 µF case fits its bracket. Increasing capacitance changes the auxiliary-winding current and motor behavior.

For a replacement, keep the specified nominal µF. A higher AC voltage rating is an option only within the motor maker’s approved replacement specification, with the same duty and suitable dimensions. A 450 VAC label describes the capacitor rating, not a requirement to run the motor from a 450 V supply.
Temperature category and installed fit

The 35 µF sample carries 40/70/21. The catalogue lists −40 to +85 °C for the series, while the selected model defines its own temperature category. Neither source establishes a universal CBB60 life class. Any Class B or other life claim needs its rated voltage, temperature and supporting model document.

Wire leads suit an assembly with a routed harness. Quick-connect blades suit a defined mating connector. A base stud changes the mounting envelope, while a twin-core cable needs its exit direction and finished length specified. The body diameter alone cannot describe these installations.

CD60 Duty Cycle: On-Time and Restart Limits | Hanxing Capacitor

A CD60 is an intermittent-duty AC motor start capacitor. Its permitted on-time and restart interval come from the selected model’s duty rating. Calculate duty cycle as energized time divided by the complete start-to-start cycle, and retain the maximum on-time as a separate limit.
The switching device ends the starting interval

A start capacitor helps the auxiliary winding produce starting torque. The motor’s switching arrangement disconnects it after startup. The relay, switch or other specified device must perform that function; using the right µF value cannot compensate for a start capacitor left connected during continuous running.

For a pump or compressor, describe the longest starting interval under the specified load and the shortest interval before another start. Automatic restart attempts after a fault belong in that description. A nominal starts-per-hour figure can hide a closely spaced group of starts.
Two sequences with the same percentage

For a calculation example, 2 seconds energized followed by 118 seconds off gives a 120-second cycle. Duty cycle is 2 ÷ 120 × 100 = 1.67%, with 30 evenly spaced starts per hour. A 3-second on-time and 177-second rest also gives 1.67%, but only 20 starts per hour. The second sequence has a longer individual energized interval.

These are arithmetic examples, not HAN XING CD60 ratings or recorded tests. KEMET’s MS/MD datasheet gives a model-specific starting-duty example and shows that voltage and frequency can change the permitted duty. Its limits cannot be transferred to a CD60 by matching the percentage alone.
Specify the worst restart pattern

A motor can take longer to accelerate under a different load. Repeated unsuccessful starts add energized time without bringing the motor to running speed. The equipment protection and switching system must handle that condition. Replacing the capacitor will not repair a failed relay or free a mechanically stalled motor.

Specify the required µF and VAC, frequency, maximum energized time, minimum rest interval and sequence of starts. Use the discharge arrangement required by the motor design, including any specified resistor, as part of the complete circuit.

Some single-phase motors use both. The motor circuit, rather than the equipment name or case shape, identifies which component you need.
Why the auxiliary winding uses a capacitor

In a capacitor motor, the capacitor changes the phase of current in the auxiliary winding relative to the main winding. The winding arrangement and phase displacement help produce the rotating magnetic field needed for torque. The motor designer selects capacitance for that winding and its intended duty.

A permanent split capacitor, or PSC, motor keeps its run capacitor in circuit for starting and running. A capacitor-start design uses a start capacitor during acceleration. A capacitor-start, capacitor-run motor includes both functions. Those arrangements explain why a run capacitor can contribute to starting even though it is not an intermittent-duty start capacitor.
Construction follows the intended duty

The HAN XING CBB60, CBB61 and CBB65 families are film motor run capacitors. Their insulated cylindrical, rectangular and metal-can formats suit different assemblies. CD60 uses an AC aluminium electrolytic construction for intermittent starting. Select each family for the duty specified in the motor circuit.

A start capacitor cannot replace a run capacitor for continuous operation. Likewise, a run capacitor with a convenient case cannot be assumed to meet a motor’s starting requirement. The approved replacement specification must cover construction, µF, VAC and duty together.
Identify the circuit before buying a replacement

For a pump with a failed external capacitor, the useful starting point is the motor model and original circuit diagram. They distinguish the permanently connected part from a switched starting component. In a two-capacitor motor, label photographs for both parts prevent the run and start ratings from being mixed in the order.

If the motor hums, turns slowly or overheats, those symptoms do not prove which component failed. Supply, wiring, mechanical load and the starting switch also affect operation. A replacement decision follows diagnosis; increasing capacitance is not a substitute for it.

Run and start capacitors have different jobs

Where a film run capacitor is fitted, it remains in the circuit during operation. Where an electrolytic start capacitor is fitted, the switching system removes it after the starting interval. A box containing both requires each original value and connection to be recorded separately.
